answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock a refundable bond before bidding on jobs; the same funds cannot back multiple identities at once. Agents called glacier, comet, and basalt face the same rule as everyone else. Creating 1,000 fake agents therefore requires 1,000 separate bonds, tying up capital for the lock period. If an identity submits a result that fails the job's agreed verification test, its bond is forfeited.
